title: Establish graceful account pool exhaustion backoff and delayed dispatch
task_summary: Prevented pool exhaustion from triggering task failures. Implemented proactive capacity checking in WorkflowEngine, holding ready tasks until capacity frees up. Added a bounded retry and backoff loop for AccountPoolExhausted in coordinator.py, and routed waiting_on_capacity status notifications to the orchestrator.

files_changed.change: Added has_capacity_for helper method to safely check capacity without state mutation.
Updated run() loop to only dispatch tasks if capacity is available, holding the rest and handling permanent pool exhaustion deadlocks gracefully.
Added bounded retry/backoff loop catching AccountPoolExhausted, notifying the orchestrator with waiting_on_capacity status on each attempt.
Added test_account_pool_exhaustion_graceful_backoff verifying oversubscribed workflows run sequentially without failure.

assumptions_verified.verification: Confirmed that oversubscribed tasks run successfully and sequentially rather than immediately failing.
Validated that 'waiting_on_capacity' status is delivered to the orchestrator instead of execution failures.

decisions.decision: Treat permanent capacity exhaustion as a deadlock failure
decisions.reasoning: If no tasks are running and none can be dispatched, capacity can never free up, so breaking the loop and marking them as failed is the correct, permanent failure response.

self_review.checked: All modified files, schema, and test executions.

notes_for_next_step: Step 9 is fully completed and thoroughly verified. The oversubscription pool backoff pipeline is fully active and tested.
